classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied bar diagrams and unitary tables to divide a total into ratio parts; the hardest parts distinguish total parts from the difference in parts to answer how many more.

inlines.text: Beth and Sven divide 40 sweets in the ratio
How many sweets does Beth receive?

spec.description: Unshaded bars with two Beth cells and three Sven cells, sharing a left baseline and equal cell widths; a right brace shows their total.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied labels and total are visible; no calculated share is shown.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}5\text{ parts}&=40\text{ sweets}\\1\text{ part}&=40\div5=8\text{ sweets}\\2\text{ parts}&=2\times8=16\text{ sweets}\end{align*}$$
Beth receives 16 sweets.

inlines.text: A 54 m long piece of timber is cut in the ratio
Find the length of the shorter piece.

spec.description: Unshaded four-cell shorter-piece bar above a five-cell longer-piece bar; aligned left ends and equal cells, with a right total brace.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied total 54 is visible; neither piece length is supplied.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}9\text{ parts}&=54\text{ m}\\1\text{ part}&=54\div9=6\text{ m}\\4\text{ parts}&=4\times6=24\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
The shorter piece is 24 m long.

inlines.text: James and Jemma scored goals in their netball game in the ratio
If they scored 56 goals total, how many more goals did James score compared to Jemma?

spec.description: James has five cells above Jemma's two equal cells. The right brace spans both bars; a lower brace spans the three-cell excess from the end of Jemma's bar to the end of James's bar.
spec.mathematics: James:Jemma = 5:2; total 56 goals; the unknown difference represents three cells.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied total 56 and unknown marker ? are visible; the calculated difference is hidden.

answer.worked:
The difference is $5-2=3$ parts.
$$\begin{align*}7\text{ parts}&=56\text{ goals}\\1\text{ part}&=56\div7=8\text{ goals}\\3\text{ parts}&=3\times8=24\text{ goals}\end{align*}$$
James scored 24 more goals than Jemma.

inlines.text: Ben buys melons and bananas in the ratio
If he buys 30 pieces of fruit in total, how many more melons did he buy?

spec.description: Unshaded seven-cell Melons bar above a three-cell Bananas bar, sharing a left baseline and equal cell widths; a right brace spans both bars.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied total 30 is visible; the shares and their difference are hidden.

answer.worked:
The difference is $7-3=4$ parts.
$$\begin{align*}10\text{ parts}&=30\text{ pieces of fruit}\\1\text{ part}&=30\div10=3\text{ pieces of fruit}\\4\text{ parts}&=4\times3=12\text{ pieces of fruit}\end{align*}$$
Ben bought 12 more melons than bananas.
